extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of 18th-century French political history; scholars of d'Argenson and Voltaire
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter of a historical/biographical work recounting the political career, journal entries, correspondence, and foreign-policy principles of the Marquis d'Argenson (c.1737–1747). Emphasis is on his motives, criticism of Cardinal Fleury, and the principles he brought to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public spirit over private ambition
rubrics_metrics.description: A public man should possess 'love of the common good' and not be driven primarily by self-aggrandisement or intrigue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Textual evidence: quote contrasting a brother who 'thinks only of himself' and seeks place 'through an underground channel' with the ideal of capacity 'recognised and employed.' Anti-pattern: seeking office by party intrigue rather than recognized capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity and straightforwardness as political virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Simplicity and straightforwardness will always be my warrant against the suspicion' of improper connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a personal standard by d'Argenson to rebut suspicions of factional ties. Implied evaluative test for a statesman: visible straightforward conduct reduces suspicion of intrigue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rancour and personal pique in political action
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish legitimate patriotic opposition from factional rancour or actions motivated by private pique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chapter frames an inquiry: whether d'Argenson's conduct was 'mere personal ambition' or 'the wise and just conviction of a patriot and an honest man.' Use historical context to judge motive rather than taking caustic language at face value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial knowledge: competence in affairs and in men
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective ministers require both knowledge of affairs of state and sound knowledge of men (personnel and character).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated criticism of Cardinal Fleury emphasises his defective 'knowledge of men' and the consequences for governance. Anti-pattern: administration staffed by men 'whose name has not to be sought for in his despatches' (i.e., lacking notable ability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess criticisms by their factual warrant
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate political criticism by checking whether it is supported by facts and whether history endorses the verdict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author asks whether d'Argenson's criticisms were factious or 'the wise and just conviction of a patriot,' and notes that 'history has endorsed his verdict' in many respects. Guidance: compare allegations to documentary evidence (despatches, journals).

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity/straightforwardness as a principle of national policy
rubrics_metrics.description: In the dealings of a great nation, the 'profoundest principle of policy was simple straightforwardness.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: D'Argenson's stated policy principle: straightforward conduct in foreign relations to allay European distrust. Use this as a normative standard when judging diplomatic actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑aggression; prioritise prosperity over territorial expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: France had 'nothing further to gain by aggression' and statesmen should henceforth focus on extending prosperity rather than borders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy recommendation: avoid further imperial expansion; promote economic and domestic wellbeing. Anti-pattern: warfare pursued for conquest rather than national prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterbalance Bourbon/Habsburg dominance via support for smaller powers (le tiers parti)
rubrics_metrics.description: France should strengthen smaller powers (Sardinia, Bavaria, Saxony, Poland, Prussia) as a counterpoise to Hapsburg and Bourbon influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic criterion: encourage independence movements and local actors as a means of containing major rivals. Example: encouragement of movements in Germany and Italy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contain Spanish ambitions in Italy while supporting Spain against English commercial aggrandisement
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactically discountenance Spanish territorial ambitions in Italy but support Spain in resisting English commercial dominance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nuanced foreign-policy prescription: friendly relations with Spain but resistance to Spanish expansion in the Italian peninsula; simultaneously oppose English attempts at commercial monopoly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of influence to weaken Habsburg power in Germany
rubrics_metrics.description: France should act to 'destroy the power of the House of Austria in Germany' and use its influence, and if necessary arms, in favour of pretenders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit strategic objective: exploit succession crises (e.g., death of Charles VI) as opportunities for partition or reduction of Habsburg influence. Anti-pattern: passive acceptance of Habsburg dominance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check Russian designs through northern alliances
rubrics_metrics.description: Russian ambitions should be checked by a defensive alliance with Sweden and Denmark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diplomatic recommendation: balance eastern powers by regional coalitions; practical focus on Scandinavian partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect colonial and commercial interests; restore naval power
rubrics_metrics.description: France must 'resolutely resist the efforts of England to establish a commercial monopoly' and be prepared to declare war rather than allow seizure of Spanish colonies; restoration of the French marine is essential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational criterion: prioritize naval rebuilding and maritime readiness as instruments of commercial and colonial policy. Example: withdraw Holland from English influence, support Spain's colonial policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for Italian reordering: expulsion of Austrians and an Italian confederation
rubrics_metrics.description: An admirable objective is 'the expulsion of the Austrians from Italy, and the surrender of the whole peninsula to an Italian confederation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as an ideal strategic goal—commended for its potential impact on Austria; noted as 'ideal' but believed feasible given prior examples (Chauvelin's actions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic priority: ten years of peace, retrenchment, and reform
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the critical condition of the French provinces, the paramount national need is 'ten years of peace, retrenchment, and reform.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy prioritisation: avoid costly wars that impoverish provinces; focus public expenditure on reform and recovery. Used to critique governments that drain provincial resources through war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judge political writings in context of authorship and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the weight of an author's published essays (e.g., the 'Essai') by their date, length, and prominence in the author's corpus; short academic essays may not reflect major practical influence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: M. Zevort's reliance on a short 'Essai' is questioned: guidance is to prefer the running Journal (longer-term writing) when attributing influence on later policy. Anti-pattern: over-weighting brief pamphlets as central evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate ministerial capacity in context of actual political power
rubrics_metrics.description: When judging a minister's apparent inconsistency or impotence, consider the external political constraints (e.g., dominance of other power brokers like Marshal de Noailles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text argues that d'Argenson's seeming 'inconsequence' may be due to lack of real power rather than personal confusion. Guidance: use institutional context and documentary evidence (despatches, Noailles’s influence) to apportion responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical diplomatic appointments must be economically supported
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment to an embassy requires sufficient emoluments to 'support the dignity of an ambassador'; lack of funds can delay or undermine diplomatic postings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by d'Argenson's delayed departure for Portugal due to emolument difficulties; evaluative test for appointments: check whether funding matches the expected cost of maintaining the post.
